description:
FOUND s493 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by a MACHINE-GENERATED name-hygiene table (#2003 generalized from the 26 exported `pl-` TAP names to the runtime's own vocabulary): every exported `p-NAME` whose NAME is a legal Perl identifier and NOT a perl builtin (36 of 210), one program each -- `sub NAME { "user:@_" } print NAME(1,2), "|", main->NAME(3), "|", &NAME(4), "\n";` (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s493/angles/hostnames/rt/, log ../rt-run.log; perl 5.40.3 vs main 093732ab).  9 same, 27 differ:

    __pcl_set_prototype aref aslice backslash backtick box can cwd decf defpackage exception flatten getcwd gethash hash hslice incf isweak let overloaded reftype regex set_up_inc setf subst typeglob weaken

MECHANISM (measured on `flatten`): the DEFINITION is right (`(p-sub pl-flatten ...)`), the method call and the `&NAME(...)` call are right, and the PLAIN CALL `NAME(args)` is emitted as `(p-NAME args)` -- the runtime's function or MACRO -- so the generic "is NAME a builtin?" test answers from the runtime's symbol list (or a table that includes internal operators) BEFORE asking whether the user declared a sub of that name.  Outcomes: `hash(1,2)` prints "12" (SILENT WRONG: the runtime's hash constructor, stringified); `flatten`/`cwd`/`box` die with a CL program error; `let`/`setf`/`regex` fail at COMPILE time inside a macro expansion (the whole file is lost).  `sub flatten`, `sub hash`, `sub box`, `sub regex`, `sub exception`, `sub cwd` are everyday names.
FIX SHAPE (rule 11: one place): the callable classifier (#266) decides -- a name the program DECLARES (or imports) is a user call `pl-NAME`, always; only a PERL builtin (perlfunc's list / `known_no_of_params`) may lower to `p-NAME`, and an internal operator name must never be reachable from a Perl identifier at all.  Find the table or predicate that makes `flatten` look builtin (grep ExprToCL's funcall lowering for the `p-` prefixing fallback) and key it on the perl builtin list, not on "the runtime has this symbol".  PROBE THE BREAKING CASE: a user sub that OVERRIDES a real builtin by name (`sub reverse {...}` called as `reverse(...)` -- perl calls the BUILTIN unless imported/`use subs`; #1870/#1992 own that), `can`/`isa` as methods, `Cwd::cwd` imported (must still reach the shim, not the user's absence).
Guard: the generator itself as a Pl/t file (names derived from the export list at test time, so a NEW runtime operator is covered the day it is added); run time ~1 s per name => batch the 36 names into ONE program with each call in its own `eval {}` once the compile-time failures are gone.  Sibling: #2003 (TAP names) -- same batch (s492b member).
ALSO CHECKED THERE, CLEAN: Perl PACKAGES named like CL packages (CL, Keyword, PCL, Sequence, List, Stream, Package, T, Nil, Uiop, Asdf ...: 16 of 16 identical) and user subs named like CL operators (t, nil, list, car, format, error, funcall, lambda, quote, function, progn, block, the, values, load, compile, intern, gensym: all right except `setf` and `let`, which are runtime names).


=== DONE (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2100: a user sub named like a RUNTIME-INTERNAL operator is the user's".

MECHANISM: ExprToCL's `%RUNTIME_NAMES` is NOT perl's builtin list -- beside `print` and `reverse` it
holds the runtime's own vocabulary (flatten hash aref aslice box setf let regex subst typeglob cwd
reftype weaken exception ...) -- and `cl_name`'s plain-call arm lowered to `p-NAME` on that table
alone, so the user's sub was never reached.  27 of the 36 such names failed: `hash(1,2)` printed
"12" (the runtime's hash constructor, stringified), `flatten`/`cwd`/`box` died with a CL program
error, and `let`/`setf`/`regex` failed inside a MACROEXPANSION, losing the whole file.  The method
call and the `&NAME(...)` form were right all along, which located the bug.

THE RULE: a name the program DECLARES (or imports) is the user's, UNLESS it is a perl KEYWORD --
perl calls the builtin for `sub reverse {...}; reverse(...)` unless it was imported or predeclared
with `use subs` (#1870/#1992 own that half, and their registry still runs first).  "Is it a keyword"
is MEASURED, not listed: prototype("CORE::NAME") DIES for a non-keyword, so the die is the
discriminator -- Pl::PExpr::Config::is_core_keyword, memoized.  "Does the program declare it" asks
the environment's prototype record, the same reading `_declared_named_unary` makes.

`CORE::NAME` NAMES THE BUILTIN UNCONDITIONALLY and had to be carried into `cl_name` as its own flag
in the same commit: PExpr's normalize pre-pass strips the prefix and leaves a `_core_qualified`
marker, and without consulting it lib/Cwd.pm's `sub cwd { CORE::cwd() }` called ITSELF and exhausted
the binding stack -- found by the BREAK-CASE probe, not by a test.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 + shapes; emission-ab over lib + the CPAN board 430 files,
19 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF, every one the SAME symbol -- a Test-Simple .t file's own `sub exception` now
reaching pl-exception instead of the runtime's p-exception.  PROBES vs perl 5.40.3: all 27 names in
one program (three call spellings each) identical, where the base was wrong on every one and died
partway; the break-case probe (Cwd, Scalar::Util, List::Util, `sub reverse`, can/isa as methods,
`ref`) is unchanged from the base row for row.
NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 10-name.
GUARD: Pl/t/runtime-name-hygiene-01.t -- the names are DERIVED from %RUNTIME_NAMES at test time, so
an operator added tomorrow is covered the day it is added; row 2 fails on a 5ce155cb extraction.
SIBLING #2003 (TAP names) does NOT share a predicate with this one -- measured: this is a COMPILER
table, #2003 is the :pcl package's export list, a RUNTIME/load-model fact.  Two mechanisms.
subject: SILENT WRONG / CRASH (name hygiene vs the RUNTIME): a user sub named like a runtime-internal operator is HIJACKED at a plain call -- `sub flatten {...} flatten(1,2)` emits `(p-flatten 1 2)`; 27 of 36 such names fail: flatten hash box let cwd getcwd can regex exception subst setf incf decf aref gethash reftype weaken typeglob ...
